footnotes: NOTE:—Apart from the foregoing obligations there are additional foreign loans in suspense, mostly without specific security and all in default. Principally amongst these are: (a) Telegraph loans: (Original amounts contracted):* [listed in p1022_2] (b) Loans made on account of Railways to be Built:* These advances were originally about £1,000,000, G$1,150,000, Francs 105,800,000, Yen 32,600,000 and Taels 3,000,000 (c) Nishihara Loans. Granted in 1917/19 under various titles against nominal security. Estimated to aggregate between Yen 150,000,000 and Yen 350,000,000 (d) Obligations incurred by various Government departments for material supplied from abroad. These debts, though not inconsiderable, are not meant to be tabulated here (e) The Boxer Indemnity. Since the enforcement of the original Boxer Protocol the following portions have been cancelled: German and Austrian. The following portions have recently been remitted for educational and other purposes for Chinese citizens, principally within the country: American, Russian, British and Japanese, These items require no exchange settlements. The French share in the Boxer Indemnity has been used for the payment of Far Eastern claims of the defunct Banque Industrielle and for educational purposes in China. Its balance has been issued in 1925 in G$ bonds. The Belgian share has been converted into G$ loan bonds of 1928, proceeds to be used to the extent of 75% for railway construction, while 25% are to be applied to educational and charitable purposes. The Italian share has been converted into a gold dollar obligation, though there was no public loan bonds issue as yet. Proceeds to be devoted to railroad construction and education. The Dutch portion (Glds 6,000 a month) is also being reserved for improvements in China.
* (For full particulars see "Foreign Loan Obligations of China" by J. R. Baylin, Peking 1925.)
